hi bobyv87,

I've been reading RTM articles and now I'm reading some journals before doing anything else.

I registered in January 2013, but at that time I was focused in other
things so I didn't pay attention to the necessary process of learning.

These last 3 weeks I've been searching knowledge with a purpose and it makes a big difference.

Having said that, analize what I'm going to write and ponder if it makes sense to you.

This is also an FTR. Why you didn't take into account this?

Look at the swing points that define FTR1. The HH at the right is also the first Swing High of FTR2.

I can see two inner ftrs (ftrs within FTR1). The right leg of the second one is the one that defines FTR1.

FTR PAZ is defined by FTR1 and FTR2

About Engulfs:

Post
 readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/journa...rnal?start=400#35777

I have some doubts about how you choose which level have to be engulfed in order to use it as confirmation.

Think in terms of Flag Limits: :Picture a Rally - Base - Rally Or Pole - FTR - Flagging if you like.

When price breaks the limit, it will likely fill the base.

Now look at what was engulfed in those charts and then look at the distance to the base.

If price engulfs the limit and retraces, entry is at DP to engulf, and target is the base of the pole.

Hope this helps.

author: Bodostock
text:
Hi, Les Paul

Sorry to post this in your journal.

But because this was your posting which i have some queries, i thought
it would be better to post it here , hoping to get some feedback from
anyone.

In posting 174, you have shared your knowledge of PAZ - compression, stacked supply/demand and zone between PAZ.

I couldn't understand the concept of stacked supply/ demand PAZ and how to really spot them.

And for another reason i do not understand is that unlike compression
where supply/demand was already consumed while on the way up or down to
the the next DP, ity was said that stacked supply and demand still has
its unfilled order left behind. So i do not understand the rationale
that when the the edge of the SPAZ was engulfed, how is it that we can
be so sure it will reach the other end of the PAZ? I mean since there
are unfilled orders at every stacked supply/demand, shouldn't we be
expecting reaction at one of the stack that could possibly bring price
back to the original direction?

I have this thinking because since stacked supply and demand has
unfilled orders and they carry on to move lower /higher, aren't they
considered as FTR and if they are considered as FTR, that's the more i
feel that price would have reaction when they retraced to the stacks
rather than engulfing every one of them all the way to the other end.

Then on this example Les Paul shown in his post 174, he showed this chart as an example of a SPAZ and how it was engulfed.

Now as per i added my comments in the chart, to me i am not sure how this looks like a stacked supply.

I thought it was a engulf of low, then price retraced but capped formed a RBD FTR.

Then as price bounced back later, it was at least to me that price was
resisted by the FTR and came down. But i am surprised to see that Les
Paul treated this contact as being an engulf of the zone.

Of course, price eventually did go back to the very top in the end.

But i just could not understand how was that an engulf.

Thank you
